prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1250; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The front bumper cover is cracked across the center and the upper grille bracket has snapped. The hood shows a shallow crease toward the driver side, and the radiator support has a slight bend that will need a sectioned replacement rather than a straight pull. The headlamp assembly on the driver side is cracked but the housing remains intact. Most of the damage lines up well with the reported impact, and the labor hours on the estimate fit the scope of this work. Nothing on the vehicle suggests earlier damage, and the parts and charges on the invoices show no repeated entries. The plan is to replace the bumper cover, grille bracket, hood, and headlamp, section and align the radiator support, and then complete a full cooling system pressure test before release.
